title: Finite Galois descent for arbitrary semilinear vector spaces
statement: Let $L/k$ be a finite Galois extension of fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]: $L$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal, meaning that every minimal polynomial over $k$ of an element of $L$ splits in $L[T]$. Put $\Pi=\operatorname{Aut}_k(L)$. A semilinear $\Pi$-action on an $L$-vector space $V$ is a family of additive bijections $\sigma_V$ with $1_V=\mathrm{id}$, $(\sigma\tau)_V=\sigma_V\tau_V$, and $\sigma_V(\lambda v)=\sigma(\lambda)\sigma_V(v)$. Put $V^\Pi=\{v\in V:\sigma_V(v)=v\text{ for all }\sigma\}$, a $k$-vector space. Scalar extension $U\mapsto L\otimes_k U$ [def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with action $\sigma(\lambda\otimes u)=\sigma(\lambda)\otimes u$, and the invariants functor are inverse equivalences between $k$-vector spaces and semilinear $\Pi$-spaces, with equivariant $L$-linear maps as morphisms. More explicitly, for every $V$ the map $\theta_V:L\otimes_k V^\Pi\to V$, $\lambda\otimes v\mapsto\lambda v$, is an equivariant $L$-linear isomorphism, natural in equivariant $L$-linear maps. For every $U$ the map $\eta_U:U\to(L\otimes_k U)^\Pi$, $u\mapsto1\otimes u$, is a natural $k$-linear isomorphism. For $k$-vector spaces $U,W$, $f\mapsto 1\otimes f$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_k(U,W)$ to the equivariant $L$-linear maps $L\otimes_k U\to L\otimes_k W$. There is no finite-dimensionality assumption on $U,V,W$.

source.place: Appendix A.64, printed pp.580–581 (all vector spaces, finite Galois case); Proposition 3.36, printed p.77 (explicit invariants quasi-inverse). Also Stacks Project Tag 0CDR, descent.tex, lemma-galois-descent, specialized to X = Spec(k), gives the equivalent quasi-coherent formulation.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field], $\Pi$ is finite and $L^\Pi=k$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition], with its base field $L$ renamed $k$ and its extension $E$ renamed $L$. Take the inverse image of the function $\delta_{\sigma,1}$ under its tensor isomorphism. By the tensor presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write it as a finite sum $\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i$. Thus $\sum_i a_i\sigma(b_i)=\delta_{\sigma,1}$ for every $\sigma\in\Pi$. For $v\in V$ set $T_b(v)=\sum_{\sigma\in\Pi}\sigma_V(bv)$. Reindexing by $\sigma\mapsto\tau\sigma$ proves $\tau_V(T_b(v))=T_b(v)$, so $T_b(v)\in V^\Pi$. Define the additive map $S_V:V\to L\otimes_k V^\Pi$ by $S_V(v)=\sum_i a_i\otimes T_{b_i}(v)$. These sums are finite independently of the dimension of $V$.

proof.text: The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the stated $L$-linear map $\theta_V$. The preceding coefficient identities give $\theta_V S_V(v)=\sum_\sigma(\sum_i a_i\sigma(b_i))\sigma_V(v)=v$. Write $\operatorname{tr}(c)=\sum_\sigma\sigma(c)$. Reindexing shows this scalar is fixed, hence lies in $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]. For $w\in V^\Pi$ and $c\in L$, tensor balancing gives $S_V(cw)=\sum_i a_i\otimes\operatorname{tr}(b_ic)w=(\sum_i a_i\operatorname{tr}(b_ic))\otimes w=c\otimes w$: indeed the coefficient in parentheses is $\sum_\sigma\sigma(c)\sum_i a_i\sigma(b_i)=c$. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove $S_V\theta_V=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\theta_V$ is bijective, and its inverse is automatically $L$-linear. On pure tensors, $\theta_V(\sigma(\lambda)\otimes w)=\sigma(\lambda)w=\sigma_V(\lambda w)$, proving equivariance. For an equivariant $L$-linear $h:V\to V\prime$, $h(\lambda w)=\lambda h(w)$ and $h(w)$ is fixed; hence $h\theta_V=\theta_{V\prime}(1\otimes h|_{V^\Pi})$. This proves naturality.

source.place: A.64, printed pp.580–581 and 3.36, printed p.77; agent-written explicit tensor calculation replacing the Morita argument, using Stacks Tags 03SF (pione-section-finite-etale-under-galois), 09DW (fields-theorem-galois-theory), 09I1 (fields-lemma-finite-Galois).

proof.text: The coefficient formula from step 1 implies $\sum_i a_i\operatorname{tr}(b_i)=1$ by summing over $\Pi$. Consequently some $\operatorname{tr}(b_j)\ne0$ (otherwise the left side is zero). Set $t=b_j/\operatorname{tr}(b_j)$, using that this denominator lies in $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field]. Then $\operatorname{tr}(t)=1$. The function $p:L\to k$, $p(c)=\operatorname{tr}(tc)$, is $k$-linear and $p(1)=1$. For any $k$-space $U$, the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] defines $P_U:L\otimes_kU\to U$ by $P_U(c\otimes u)=p(c)u$. It satisfies $P_U(1\otimes u)=u$. Moreover for every tensor $z$, $1\otimes P_U(z)=\sum_\sigma\sigma(t)\sigma(z)$, where each $\sigma$ acts on the first tensor factor: check this on $c\otimes u$, obtaining $\sum_\sigma\sigma(tc)\otimes u=1\otimes\operatorname{tr}(tc)u$, and extend additively. If $z$ is fixed this is $(\sum_\sigma\sigma(t))z=z$. Thus $P_U$ restricted to invariants is the inverse of $\eta_U$; no basis or finite-dimensionality is needed.

source.place: A.64, printed pp.580–581 and 3.36, printed p.77; agent-written explicit tensor calculation replacing the Morita argument, using Stacks Tags 03SF (pione-section-finite-etale-under-galois), 09DW (fields-theorem-galois-theory), 09I1 (fields-lemma-finite-Galois).

proof.text: The map $\eta_U$ is $k$-linear by bilinearity, takes values in invariants because $\sigma(1)=1$, and is natural since $(1\otimes f)(1\otimes u)=1\otimes f(u)$; step 3 proves it is an isomorphism. Tensoring preserves identity and composition by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and restriction to invariants does likewise. Step 2 and step 3 therefore give natural inverse isomorphisms for the two composite functors, proving the equivalence. Their standard triangle identities can also be checked directly: $\theta_{L\otimes U}(\lambda\otimes\eta_U(u))=\lambda\otimes u$; and, for fixed $w\in V$, $\theta_V(\eta_{V^\Pi}(w))=w$.

source.place: A.64, printed pp.580–581 and 3.36, printed p.77; agent-written explicit tensor calculation replacing the Morita argument, using Stacks Tags 03SF (pione-section-finite-etale-under-galois), 09DW (fields-theorem-galois-theory), 09I1 (fields-lemma-finite-Galois).

proof.text: For an equivariant $L$-linear $g:L\otimes_kU\to L\otimes_kW$, $g(1\otimes u)$ is fixed. Define $f=\eta_W^{-1}\circ g|_{(L\otimes U)^\Pi}\circ\eta_U$. It is $k$-linear. Then $g(\lambda\otimes u)=\lambda g(1\otimes u)=\lambda\eta_W(f(u))=\lambda\otimes f(u)$, so tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $g=1\otimes f$. Conversely $1\otimes f$ is equivariant on each pure tensor, and the displayed construction recovers $f$ by $\eta_W^{-1}\eta_W=\mathrm{id}$. This proves the asserted Hom bijection for arbitrary $U,W$.
